prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Baytown, Texas, and has neck strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1100; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement is for the claim file. Can you please state your full name for the record?

A: Sure. I'd rather keep my name out of the file, if that's okay. I'm the driver of the blue sedan.

Q: That's fine, we can refer to you as the claimant. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the collision?

A: I was heading down the two-lane road toward the shopping center around mid-afternoon. A pickup came over into my lane while it was passing a slow car. I braked and steered right, but we still hit nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was enough to jolt me.

Q: What was your speed when you saw the pickup?

A: I'd guess maybe twenty-five or thirty. It's a residential stretch, so I wasn't going fast.

Q: Did either vehicle's airbags deploy?

A: No, nothing deployed. Both cars drove off under their own power, though mine had to be towed later because the front bumper was pushed in.

Q: Did you seek medical attention after the collision?

A: I went to urgent care that same evening. My neck was stiff and sore, and I had some tightness across my shoulders. They diagnosed a neck strain and told me to rest and take anti-inflammatories.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes, it's better than it was, but I still get stiffness when I turn my head quickly, and I've had a few headaches. I'm doing physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Only that I want to make sure the other driver's insurer knows I was not at fault. I was in my own lane the whole time.

Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
